scope: Evidence for detailed AIR Cuttack article; read-only canonical repo. Reused cinema-radio dossier and expanded firsthand/institutional sources.

sources.title: A visit to AIR Cuttack & others
sources.author: Jose Jacob,VU2JOS
sources.kind: Firsthand station visit with assistant station engineer, not official commissioning register
claims: Dates inauguration28January1948; temporary Madhapur House studio and1kW transmitter at KillaFort.
Describes1977 studio complex with separate talk,drama,music,dubbing and playback spaces.
Observed computers alongside reel-to-reel tapes during2008visit.
Reports1999cyclone transmission interruption and emergency transmitter arrangements; author had seen fallen tower during emergency amateur-radio work.
Describes DTH studio/channel begun2006; useful changing-technology example.
limits: Keep all present-tense equipment/staff/frequency details explicitly historical2008.
Do not adopt exact equipment chronology without attribution to visitor account.
Source spells Madhapur; do not silently change to Madhupur without corroboration.

sources.title: Gopal Chhotray—South Asian Literary Recordings Project
sources.kind: Library of Congress author recording profile/catalogue
claims: Credits late1940s geetinatya revival and long AIR Cuttack association.
Documents plays,operas,shortplays and screenplays; translations across languages.
Offers author readings from Pheria,Parakalama and SeiPhula with edition metadata.
limits: Do not call these AIR performances: they are LoC literary readings.
Pheria1946writing in Bibhaba vs1947publication in LoC need not conflict; do not conflate.
Previously used in flagship; aggregate derived budget must account for repeated use.

sources.title: Gopal Chhotray collection
claims: Association with AIR from1948 beginning.
Srimati Samarjani opera adapts FakirMohanSenapati’s PatentMedicine.
Digitised collection includes plays,oneacts,gitinatya,unpublished manuscripts.
Catalogue displays ଶ୍ରୀମତୀ ସମାର୍ଜନୀ (୧୯୭୪);1974 is listed edition date, not established first broadcast.
limits: Archive biography says around500airedplays/manymanuscriptslost: omit quantitative claim unless useful and explicitly attributed.
Do not invent music credit for this opera from this page.
Cataloguedbook availability does not establish permission to reproduce pages.

sources.title: In Conversation with Odia Lyricist Devdas Chhotray
sources.author: Shyamanuja Das
sources.locator: PartII studio-stage exchange lines81–82; PartIII lines88–96
claims: Devdas remembers his first recorded ghazal Sneha Ta Bahuta Milila Jeevane,Prema Rahigala Baki as composed and sung by AkshayaMohanty for AIR Cuttack.
He distinguishes studio performance without immediate audience response from stage repetition/emphasis shaped by listeners.
Recalls limited studio instrumentation compared with later stage ensembles.
Says these ghazals were classed as adhunika in AIR programmes and records.
Recalls film songs via VividhBharati introducing him to ghazal expression.
limits: Do not call this first-ever Odia ghazal or first song he wrote; he explicitly cannot recall his first written ghazal.
Avoid quoting more than10words of song lyric; title is14words so paraphrase title or omit fulltext quotation.
His opinion about virtual demise of AIR is not institutional closure or presentfact.
Devdas and Gopal Chhotray are distinct contributors.
Do not adopt erroneous agape/eros Latin claim or MughalTamasha extinction claim.

sources.title: Shyamamani Devi on Odissi Music and Her Life as a Singer
sources.date: Mirror shows20June2013; original interview date not established.
sources.access: Mirrored interview text opened; opening section read, not originalhostPDF.
sources.locator: Early Life and Musical Influences, opening textlines76–187
claims: Describes family musical support alongside opposition from relatives to a girl singing publicly.
Recalls becoming an Akashvani child artist in1950.
Names KalicharanPattanayak’s encouragement and her continued determination.
limits: AIR station not named in this exact opening passage; Cuttack identification should be corroborated separately.
Source is interview mirror labelled OAiD; no independent original publication/date verification.
Do not generalise her personal experience to all women.
Do not adopt her honorific founder-of-Odissi assertion as historical fact.

editorial_plan: Begin with a listener imagined only as explanatory framing, not invented historical scene.
Opening1948 and specialised spaces for voice/music/drama.
Shyamamani: attributed personal perspective on opportunity and barriers.
Devdas/Akshaya: collaboration and concrete studio-stage difference.
Technology and transmission resilience through dated2008visitor account.
Present onlinebulletins and archival access; distinguish preservedbooks from survivingaudio.

No claim to exhaustive contributor roster,women’s history,listenership,or full archive survival.
